inputs.name: profile
inputs.description: Profile to scan against: cis_level1_server, cis_level2_server, stig or standard, which the circuit maps to each distribution's own profile ID, or any profile ID in the host's content, such as "anssi_bp28_high".

inputs.name: content_version
inputs.description: SCAP Security Guide release from ComplianceAsCode to scan with on Ubuntu, Debian and Fedora. Rocky Linux uses its own scap-security-guide package.

inputs.name: content_sha256
inputs.description: SHA-256 of scap-security-guide-<content_version>.zip. Change it with content_version.

inputs.name: schedule
inputs.description: When the scan timer runs, as a systemd OnCalendar expression such as "Sun 03:00" or "daily". null leaves out the timer.

inputs.name: keep
inputs.description: Number of scans to keep under /var/lib/conn3x-scap. Older ones are deleted after each scan.

inputs.name: run_now
inputs.description: Scan during the apply: on the first apply, and again whenever the scan's settings change. A scan takes minutes.

inputs.name: skip_rules
inputs.description: Rules to leave out of the profile, by ID, such as ["sshd_disable_root_login"]. The circuit writes a tailoring file that turns them off.

inputs.name: tailoring
inputs.description: Contents of your own XCCDF tailoring file, such as file("tailoring.xml"). Set profile to the ID of the tailored profile in it. Can't be used with skip_rules.

inputs.name: remediate
inputs.description: Fix what the profile finds, once per host and profile. This changes SSH, PAM, the firewall and more. Try it on a throwaway host first.
